w1-q1: Incorrect — the ITU report expects humans to become a minority of traffic generators, not to stop using the Internet.
Correct — the report foresees most traffic flowing between devices and things, which is what makes the future Internet wider and more complex.
Incorrect — the future Internet is expected to connect many kinds of devices and things, not only desktop computers.
Incorrect — Internet communication is expected to broaden to many applications, not be restricted to email.
w1-q2: Correct — IoT systems need an efficient and scalable architecture to support very large numbers of devices.
Correct — unambiguous naming and addressing is needed so each device can be identified and reached.
Correct — IoT must handle heterogeneous devices such as sleeping nodes, mobile nodes and non-IP devices.
Incorrect — IoT devices may have intermittent connectivity, so continuous connectivity at all times cannot be guaranteed.
w1-q3: Incorrect — Smart Dust is about tiny sensing hardware, not a cloud storage model.
Incorrect — Smart Dust is not a router; it consists of extremely small computing devices.
Correct — Smart Dust means extremely small computing devices, smaller than a grain of sand, used for sensing such as soil chemicals or body diagnostics.
Incorrect — Smart Dust is a physical device concept, not a type of IPv6 address.
w1-q4: Incorrect — M2M and IoT are related but not identical; IoT has a wider scope of interactions.
Incorrect — it is the reverse: M2M focuses on machine communication, while IoT also includes people and applications.
Correct — M2M mainly covers communication among machines, and is a part of the broader IoT, which also involves people, applications and systems.
Incorrect — IoT does include machine-to-machine interaction; M2M is a part of it.
w1-q5: Incorrect — the statement is false; sensors are not replaced by cloud databases in the Web of Things.
Correct — sensors remain responsible for collecting physical-world data, while web technologies expose and access IoT resources.
w1-q6: Incorrect — reusing local addresses reduces address consumption rather than increasing it.
Correct — locally valid addresses can be reused under different gateways, which avoids wasting global addresses and conserves address space.
Incorrect — the gateway is still needed to connect the local domain to the wider network.
Incorrect — gateways still allow devices to communicate with the Internet; local addressing does not prevent this.
w1-q7: Correct — IoT gateways provide Internet connectivity for the devices behind them.
Correct — gateways also support intra-connectivity within the IoT LAN.
Correct — a gateway may obtain upstream address prefixes using mechanisms such as DHCPv6.
Correct — a gateway may delegate addresses to nodes using SLAAC.
w1-q8: Incorrect — dotted decimal notation is used by IPv4, while IPv6 uses hexadecimal notation.
Incorrect — IPv6 has a much larger address space (128-bit) than IPv4 (32-bit).
Correct — IPv6 uses 128-bit addresses in hexadecimal notation, giving a far larger address space suited to large-scale IoT.
Incorrect — IPv6 does not use broadcast addresses the way IPv4 does.
w1-q9: Incorrect — a good sensor should not significantly influence the property it measures.
Incorrect — a good sensor should be insensitive to unrelated physical properties.
Correct — a good sensor responds to the measured property, ignores unrelated ones, and does not alter the measured quantity.
Incorrect — a sensor must give output that reflects the measured quantity, not random output.
w1-q10: Correct — resolution is the smallest change in the measured quantity that the sensor can detect.
Correct — for a digital sensor, resolution relates to the smallest step in its digital output.
Incorrect — resolution and accuracy are different; a high-resolution sensor can still be inaccurate due to bias or calibration error.
Correct — accuracy also depends on factors such as bias and calibration, not only on resolution.
w1-q11: Correct — an accelerometer measures acceleration along x, y and z axes, giving magnitude and direction, so it is a vector sensor.
Incorrect — an accelerometer is a vector sensor because its output has directional components, so the statement is true.
w1-q12: Incorrect — quantization error comes from representing a continuous value in discrete digital steps, not from approach direction.
Correct — hysteresis error means the output depends on input history, differing when the input is approached from below or above.
Incorrect — IPv6 translation error is not a sensor error type.
Incorrect — this is not a sensor error type; an output that depends on whether the input was approached from below or above is hysteresis error.
w1-q13: Incorrect — the statement is true, so False is wrong; hydraulic actuators can exert large forces.
Correct — hydraulic actuators use nearly incompressible liquid to transmit force, so they can exert considerable force.

Correct — high strain recovery is a known feature of shape memory polymers.
Correct — shape memory polymers can have low density and biocompatibility.
